original.title: Sauerbraten
original.description: Germany's famous sweet-and-sour pot roast: beef marinated for several days in spiced vinegar and wine, then braised and served with a gingersnap gravy.
ingredients: 3 1/2 lb beef bottom round or chuck roast
steps: Combine the vinegar, wine, water, onion, carrot, bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves, juniper, sugar and salt in a saucepan and bring to a boil, then let cool completely.
Place the beef in a deep glass or ceramic dish or zip-top bag, pour the cooled marinade over it, cover and refrigerate for 3 to 5 days, turning the meat once a day.
Remove the beef from the marinade, pat it dry with paper towels, and strain the marinade, reserving both the liquid and the vegetables.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef well on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Add the reserved vegetables and 2 cups of the strained marinade, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook over low heat (or in a 325°F (165°C) oven) for 3 to 3 1/2 hours until very tender.
Transfer the meat to a cutting board and tent it with foil to rest.
Strain the cooking liquid into a saucepan, pressing on the vegetables, and add water or more marinade to make about 2 1/2 cups.
Bring the liquid to a simmer and whisk in the gingersnaps, brown sugar and raisins, cooking for 5 to 8 minutes until the gravy is smooth and thickened.
Slice the beef against the grain and serve with the gravy, red cabbage and potato dumplings or spaetzle.

original.title: Rinderrouladen (Beef Rolls)
original.description: Thin slices of beef spread with mustard and rolled around bacon, onion and pickle, then braised in a rich brown gravy — a German Sunday dinner classic.
ingredients: 8 thin slices beef top round (about 2 lb total), pounded to 1/4 inch
2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp cold water
steps: Lay the beef slices flat, season with salt and pepper, and spread each one with 1 teaspoon of mustard.
Place a slice of bacon, a spoonful of chopped onion and a pickle spear at the short end of each slice.
Roll the beef up tightly, tucking in the sides, and secure each roll with toothpicks or kitchen twine.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the rolls on all sides, then remove them to a plate.
Add the carrot, celery and any remaining onion to the pot and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute more.
Pour in the wine, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the broth and bay leaf, return the rolls to the pot, cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours until the beef is tender.
Remove the rolls and strain or purée the sauce, then bring it to a boil and whisk in the cornstarch slurry to thicken.
Remove the toothpicks or twine and serve the rouladen with the gravy, red cabbage and boiled potatoes or dumplings.

original.title: Käsespätzle (Cheese Spaetzle)
original.description: Swabian and Allgäu comfort food: homemade egg spaetzle layered with melted mountain cheese and topped with crisp fried onions.
ingredients: 1/2 cup water or milk, as needed
steps: Whisk the flour, salt and nutmeg in a bowl, then beat in the eggs and enough water to make a thick, sticky batter, and beat with a wooden spoon until bubbles form; let rest 10 minutes.
Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onions slowly, stirring often, for 15 to 20 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a baking dish.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and press the batter through a spaetzle maker or the holes of a colander into the water in batches.
When the spaetzle float to the surface (1 to 2 minutes), lift them out with a slotted spoon and drain well.
Layer one third of the hot spaetzle in the baking dish, sprinkle with one third of the cheese and some pepper, and repeat twice.
Dot with the remaining butter and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Top with the fried onions and chives and serve immediately with a green salad.

original.title: Apfelstrudel (Apple Strudel)
original.description: Paper-thin layers of buttery pastry wrapped around cinnamon apples, raisins and toasted breadcrumbs, dusted with powdered sugar.
ingredients: 2 lb tart apples (such as Granny Smith), peeled, cored and thinly sliced
1/3 cup raisins, soaked in 2 tbsp rum or warm water
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toast the breadcrumbs in 2 tablespoons of the melted butter in a skillet over medium heat until golden, then set aside.
Toss the apples with the sugar, drained raisins, nuts, cinnamon and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Lay one sheet of phyllo on a clean kitchen towel, brush it with butter, and repeat with the remaining sheets, stacking them.
Sprinkle the toasted breadcrumbs over the lower two thirds of the stack, leaving a 2-inch border on the sides.
Spread the apple filling over the breadcrumbs, fold in the sides, and use the towel to help roll the pastry up into a tight log.
Transfer the strudel seam side down to the baking sheet and brush it generously with the remaining butter.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden brown, then let cool for 15 minutes.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm with vanilla sauce, whipped cream or ice cream.

original.title: Bienenstich (Bee Sting Cake)
original.description: A soft yeast cake topped with a crunchy honey-almond caramel and filled with vanilla pastry cream.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and softened butter and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Press the dough evenly into a greased 9 x 13-inch pan or 10-inch springform pan, cover and let rise 20 minutes.
For the topping, melt the butter, sugar, honey and cream in a saucepan, simmer for 3 minutes, stir in the almonds and let cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C), spread the almond topping over the dough, and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden.
For the filling, heat 1 1/2 cups of milk with the sugar, whisk the remaining milk with the cornstarch and yolks, then whisk this into the hot milk and cook until very thick.
Stir the vanilla into the pastry cream, cover the surface with plastic wrap and chill completely.
Cool the cake, then split it horizontally into two layers, cutting the top layer into 12 pieces.
Fold the whipped cream into the cold pastry cream, spread it over the bottom layer, set the topping pieces on top and chill for 1 hour before serving.

original.title: Rote Grütze (Red Berry Pudding)
original.description: A northern German summer dessert of red berries and currants simmered with juice and lightly thickened, served cold with vanilla sauce or cream.
ingredients: 4 cups mixed red berries (raspberries, red currants, strawberries, cherries), fresh or frozen
1 1/2 cups red berry or cherry juice
1 cup heavy cream or vanilla sauce, for serving
steps: Halve any large strawberries and pit the cherries if using fresh.
Whisk 1/4 cup of the juice with the cornstarch until smooth.
Bring the remaining juice and the sugar to a boil in a saucepan.
Add the cornstarch mixture and stir constantly until the juice thickens and turns glossy, about 1 minute.
Stir in the berries, lemon juice and vanilla and simmer for just 1 to 2 minutes so the fruit keeps its shape.
Pour into a serving bowl or individual glasses and let cool, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
Serve cold with pouring cream, vanilla sauce or vanilla ice cream.

original.title: Kartoffelpuffer (Potato Pancakes)
original.description: Crisp, lacy fried potato pancakes served with applesauce — a favorite at German Christmas markets and fairs.
steps: Grate the potatoes and onion on the coarse side of a box grater.
Place the grated mixture in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Transfer to a bowl and mix in the eggs, flour, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Heat about 1/4 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Drop 1/4-cup portions of the batter into the oil and flatten them into thin 4-inch rounds.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden brown and crisp at the edges.
Drain on paper towels and keep warm in a 200°F (95°C) oven while frying the rest, adding oil as needed.
Serve hot with applesauce, or with sour cream and smoked salmon for a savory version.

original.title: Königsberger Klopse (Meatballs in Caper Sauce)
original.description: Tender poached veal and pork meatballs in a creamy white sauce sharpened with capers and lemon, a beloved dish from old East Prussia.
ingredients: 1 stale white roll or 2 slices white bread
steps: Soak the bread in the milk for 10 minutes, then squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl.
Add the ground meats, chopped onion, egg, anchovies, salt and pepper and mix well.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into 12 to 16 meatballs about 2 inches across.
Bring the water to a boil with the bay leaf, halved onion and 1 teaspoon salt, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Add the meatballs and poach for 15 minutes, then remove them with a slotted spoon and strain and reserve 3 cups of the broth.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the reserved broth and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, capers, lemon juice and sugar, then remove from the heat and whisk a little sauce into the egg yolk before stirring it back in.
Return the meatballs to the sauce to warm through without boiling, then season to taste.
Serve with boiled potatoes and pickled beets.

original.title: Bratkartoffeln (German Fried Potatoes)
original.description: Sliced boiled potatoes fried in a cast-iron pan with bacon and onions until crisp and golden.
ingredients: 2 lb waxy potatoes (such as Yukon Gold)
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 20 minutes until just tender, then drain and let cool completely, ideally overnight.
Peel the potatoes and slice them about 1/4 inch thick.
Cook the bacon in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat until crisp, then remove it, leaving the fat in the pan.
Add the butter to the pan, then add the potatoes in a single layer and fry without stirring for 5 to 7 minutes until golden on the bottom.
Turn the potatoes and continue frying, turning occasionally, for another 10 minutes until crisp all over.
Add the onion and caraway and fry for 5 minutes more until the onion is soft and browned.
Return the bacon to the pan, season with salt and pepper, sprinkle with parsley and serve with fried eggs or bratwurst.

original.title: Rotkohl (Braised Red Cabbage)
original.description: Sweet-and-sour red cabbage slowly braised with apples, onion and warm spices — the essential side for roasts and holiday dinners.
ingredients: 1 medium head red cabbage (about 2 1/2 lb), cored and thinly sliced
2 tart apples, peeled, cored and diced
3 tbsp brown sugar or red currant jelly
steps: Melt the butter in a large heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the apples and cook for 2 minutes more.
Add the cabbage, vinegar, water, brown sugar, salt and pepper and toss well.
Tie the bay leaf, cloves and juniper in a piece of cheesecloth, or add them loose, and tuck them into the cabbage.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook over low heat for 1 to 1 1/4 hours, stirring occasionally and adding a splash of water if it gets dry.
Remove the spices and adjust the balance of sugar, vinegar and salt to taste.
Serve hot with roast pork, sauerbraten, duck or goose; it tastes even better reheated the next day.

original.title: Käsekuchen (German Cheesecake)
original.description: A light, tangy German cheesecake made with quark on a simple shortcrust base, less dense than the American style.
ingredients: 2 lb quark (or 1 1/2 lb whole-milk ricotta plus 8 oz cream cheese, blended smooth)
steps: Rub the flour, sugar, salt and butter together until crumbly, then mix in the egg yolk and knead briefly into a dough.
Press the dough into the bottom and 1 1/2 inches up the sides of a greased 9-inch springform pan and chill for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Beat the quark, sugar, egg yolks, melted butter, sour cream, cornstarch, lemon juice, zest and vanilla until smooth.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the cheese mixture.
Pour the filling into the crust and smooth the top.
Bake for 65 to 75 minutes until the top is golden and the center is just set, covering loosely with foil if it browns too fast.
Turn off the oven, prop the door open and let the cake cool inside for 1 hour to prevent cracking, then chill for at least 4 hours before slicing.

original.title: Glühwein (Mulled Wine)
original.description: The warming spiced red wine sold at every German Christmas market, scented with orange, cinnamon, cloves and star anise.
steps: Combine the water, sugar, orange and lemon slices and all of the spices in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes to dissolve the sugar and release the flavors.
Pour in the wine and heat gently over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, never letting it boil.
Taste and add more sugar if you like it sweeter.
Stir in the rum or brandy just before serving, if using.
Strain into mugs and garnish each with a fresh orange slice.

original.title: Jägerschnitzel (Hunter's Schnitzel)
original.description: Pan-fried pork cutlets smothered in a creamy mushroom and onion gravy.
ingredients: 4 boneless pork loin cutlets (about 5 oz each)
steps: Pound the cutlets between sheets of plastic wrap to 1/4 inch thick and season with salt and pepper.
Set up three shallow dishes with flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs, and dredge each cutlet in the flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry the cutlets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden, then drain and keep warm.
In another skillet, cook the bacon until crisp, then add the butter and onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute, then add the broth and simmer until thickened.
Stir in the cream, simmer for 2 minutes and season with salt, pepper and parsley.
Spoon the sauce over the schnitzel and serve with spaetzle, fries or Bratkartoffeln.

original.title: Christstollen (Christmas Stollen)
original.description: A rich, buttery fruit bread studded with rum-soaked raisins, candied peel and almonds, coated in powdered sugar.
steps: Soak the raisins and candied peel in the rum overnight or for at least 2 hours.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, spices and lemon zest, then add the milk, egg and softened butter and knead for 8 to 10 minutes into a smooth dough.
Knead in the drained fruit and the almonds, cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 1/2 hours.
Divide the dough in half and roll each piece into an oval about 10 x 8 inches.
If using marzipan, roll it into two logs and lay one down the center of each oval.
Fold one long side over past the center to form the classic stollen shape and press the edge lightly.
Place the loaves on a lined baking sheet, cover and let rise for 45 minutes while you preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Bake for 40 to 50 minutes until deep golden and the internal temperature reaches 190°F (88°C).
Brush the hot loaves generously with melted butter, dust heavily with powdered sugar, and repeat once they cool.
Wrap tightly and let the stollen mature for at least 3 days and up to 3 weeks before slicing.

original.title: Beer-Braised Bratwurst with Onions
original.description: Bratwurst simmered in lager with onions, then browned and served on crusty rolls with mustard — perfect for Oktoberfest.
ingredients: 2 bottles (12 oz each) German lager or Märzen beer
steps: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onions for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the beer, caraway and pepper and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the bratwurst, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, turning once, until cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Remove the sausages and continue simmering the onions until the beer has reduced to a thick glaze.
Meanwhile brown the bratwurst on a hot grill or in a skillet for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until well browned.
Split the rolls, add a bratwurst to each, and top with the beer onions, mustard and sauerkraut.

original.title: Currywurst
original.description: Berlin's iconic street food: sliced fried sausage drenched in a sweet, tangy curry-ketchup sauce and dusted with curry powder.
ingredients: 2 tsp curry powder, plus more for sprinkling
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the curry powder and paprika and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the ketchup, tomato sauce, vinegar, Worcestershire, honey and water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend the sauce smooth with an immersion blender if you like and keep it warm.
Heat the oil in a skillet and fry the sausages for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and heated through.
Slice the sausages into thick coins, pour the warm sauce over them and dust with more curry powder.
Serve with French fries or a crusty roll.

original.title: Kartoffelsuppe (German Potato Soup)
original.description: A hearty, rustic potato soup with leeks, root vegetables and marjoram, finished with sliced wieners.
ingredients: 1 leek, white and light green parts, sliced
1 celery root (about 8 oz), peeled and diced
2 lb starchy potatoes, peeled and diced
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until it renders its fat.
Add the butter, onion and leek and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the carrots, celery root and potatoes and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the broth, add the bay leaf, marjoram, salt and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 25 minutes until the vegetables are very tender.
Remove the bay leaf and mash or blend about half of the soup to thicken it, leaving some chunks.
Stir in the cream, nutmeg and sliced wieners and heat for 5 minutes until the sausages are hot.
Adjust the seasoning and serve sprinkled with parsley and with dark bread on the side.

original.title: Erbsensuppe (Split Pea Soup with Smoked Sausage)
original.description: A thick German split pea stew with smoked pork and vegetables, traditional at field kitchens and winter festivals.
ingredients: 1 lb dried green split peas, rinsed
1 smoked ham hock or 8 oz smoked pork belly
4 smoked sausages (such as Mettwurst or kielbasa), sliced
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the split peas, water, ham hock and bay leaf and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat, cover partially and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the carrots, leek, potatoes and marjoram and simmer for another 30 minutes until the peas have broken down.
Remove the ham hock, pull the meat from the bone, chop it and return it to the pot.
Add the sliced sausage and simmer for 10 minutes more, adding water if the soup is too thick.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with crusty bread and a little mustard.

original.title: Zwetschgenkuchen (Plum Sheet Cake)
original.description: A late-summer yeast sheet cake covered in rows of halved Italian plums and finished with cinnamon sugar or streusel.
ingredients: 3 lb Italian prune plums, halved and pitted
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the milk, egg and butter, and knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Grease a 12 x 17-inch rimmed baking sheet and roll or press the dough evenly into it.
Cut a small slit into the top of each plum half so it fans open slightly.
Arrange the plums cut side up in tight overlapping rows over the dough.
Let rise for 20 minutes while you preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the dough is golden and the plums are juicy.
Brush with melted butter, sprinkle with the mixed cinnamon and sugar, and serve warm or cool with whipped cream.

original.title: Obatzda (Bavarian Beer Cheese Spread)
original.description: A tangy Bavarian beer-garden spread of ripe Camembert, butter, paprika and beer, served with pretzels and radishes.
ingredients: 8 oz ripe Camembert or Brie, rind on, chopped
steps: Mash the Camembert with a fork in a bowl until mostly smooth with a few small chunks.
Add the softened butter and cream cheese and mash until well combined.
Stir in the onion, paprika, caraway, salt and pepper.
Add the beer a little at a time until the spread is creamy but not runny.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour so the flavors blend.
Mound the obatzda on a plate, dust with a little more paprika, sprinkle with chives and serve with soft pretzels, rye bread and radishes.

original.title: Maultaschen (Swabian Filled Pasta)
original.description: Large Swabian pasta pockets filled with meat, spinach and herbs, served in broth or pan-fried with onions.
ingredients: 10 oz frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
4 oz smoked ham or bratwurst meat, finely chopped
1 stale roll, soaked in water and squeezed
steps: Mix the flour, eggs, salt and water into a firm dough, knead for 8 minutes until smooth, then wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Melt the butter and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then let cool.
Combine the onion with the spinach, ground pork, ham, soaked roll, egg, parsley, salt, pepper and nutmeg and mix well.
Divide the dough in half and roll each piece into a thin rectangle about 12 x 16 inches.
Spread half of the filling over the lower half of each sheet, leaving a border, then fold the top half over.
Press firmly with the handle of a wooden spoon at 3-inch intervals to seal, then cut into squares along the pressed lines.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and cook the Maultaschen for 12 to 15 minutes until the filling is cooked through.
Serve them in bowls of hot broth sprinkled with chives, or slice leftovers and fry them in butter with onions and egg.

original.title: Frikadellen (German Pan-Fried Meat Patties)
original.description: Juicy pan-fried patties of beef and pork with onion, mustard and marjoram, eaten hot or cold with potato salad.
ingredients: 1 stale roll or 2 slices white bread
steps: Soak the roll in the milk for 10 minutes, then squeeze it out well.
Combine the bread with the ground beef, pork, onion, egg, mustard, marjoram, parsley, salt, pepper and paprika and knead until evenly mixed.
Shape the mixture into 8 slightly flattened patties about 3/4 inch thick.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry the patties for 5 to 7 minutes per side until well browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot with potatoes and gravy, or cold with mustard and potato salad.

original.title: Himmel und Erde (Heaven and Earth)
original.description: A Rhineland dish of mashed potatoes and apples ('earth' and 'heaven') topped with fried blood sausage or bratwurst and crisp onions.
ingredients: 2 lb starchy potatoes, peeled and cubed
2 tart apples, peeled, cored and chopped
1 lb blood sausage (Blutwurst) or bratwurst, sliced thick
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile simmer the apples with the sugar, lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of water for 10 minutes until soft.
Drain the potatoes and mash them with 2 tablespoons of butter, the warm milk, salt and nutmeg.
Fold the cooked apples into the mashed potatoes, keeping some texture.
Fry the bacon in a skillet until crisp, then add the onions and cook until golden and caramelized; remove and keep warm.
In the same pan, melt the remaining butter and fry the sausage slices for 2 to 3 minutes per side until crisp.
Spoon the potato-apple mash onto plates and top with the sausage, onions and bacon.

original.title: Gurkensalat (German Cucumber Salad)
original.description: Thinly sliced cucumbers in a light dill and sour cream dressing — a cool side for schnitzel and summer meals.
steps: Toss the cucumber slices with the salt in a colander and let them drain for 20 minutes.
Squeeze the cucumbers gently to remove excess liquid.
Whisk together the sour cream, vinegar, sugar, pepper and dill in a bowl.
Add the cucumbers and onion and toss to coat.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving and taste for salt.

original.title: Versunkener Apfelkuchen (Sunken Apple Cake)
original.description: A simple buttery sponge cake baked with scored apple halves that sink into the batter as it bakes.
ingredients: 1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp unsalted butter, softened
4 small apples, peeled, halved and cored
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Cut several shallow parallel slits into the rounded side of each apple half and brush with lemon juice.
Beat the butter, sugar, vanilla and lemon zest until light and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt together and fold into the batter alternately with the milk.
Spread the batter into the pan and press the apple halves, scored side up, lightly into the surface.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer inserted in the cake comes out clean.
Brush the warm apples with apricot jam, let cool in the pan, then dust with powdered sugar before serving.

original.title: Pfeffernüsse (Spice Cookies)
original.description: Small, round Christmas cookies spiced with pepper, cinnamon, cloves and anise and glazed with powdered sugar.
steps: Warm the honey, brown sugar and butter in a saucepan until melted, then let cool to lukewarm.
Beat the egg into the honey mixture.
Whisk together the flour, almonds, baking soda, spices and salt, then stir in the honey mixture to form a stiff dough.
Cover and chill the dough for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line baking sheets with parchment.
Roll the dough into 1-inch balls and place them 1 inch apart on the sheets.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until firm and lightly browned on the bottom, then cool completely.
Whisk the powdered sugar and milk into a thin glaze, dip each cookie, and let the glaze set on a rack.

original.title: Dampfnudeln (Steamed Yeast Dumplings)
original.description: Fluffy yeast buns steamed in a covered pan with milk and butter until they form a golden caramel crust on the bottom, served with vanilla sauce.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm milk, egg and butter, and knead for 8 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, shape them into smooth balls, cover and let rise for 20 minutes.
In a wide heavy pan with a tight-fitting glass lid, heat the milk, butter and sugar until the butter melts.
Place the dough balls in the pan, cover tightly, and cook over medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes without lifting the lid, until the liquid is absorbed and you hear crackling.
Meanwhile, whisk 1/2 cup milk with the cornstarch and yolks, heat the remaining milk and sugar, whisk in the cornstarch mixture and cook until thickened, then add the vanilla.
Remove the lid, loosen the dumplings and serve them caramel side up with the warm vanilla sauce or stewed plums.

original.title: Brötchen (German Bread Rolls)
original.description: Crusty, airy German breakfast rolls with a crackly crust, perfect for butter, jam, cheese and cold cuts.
ingredients: 1 egg white beaten with 1 tbsp water
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, salt and sugar, then add the water and oil and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let the dough rise for 1 1/2 hours until doubled.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, shape each into a tight ball, and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Cover and let rise for 30 to 40 minutes until puffy.
Place an empty metal pan on the bottom rack and preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Brush the rolls with egg white, sprinkle with seeds if desired, and cut a deep slash across the top of each with a sharp knife.
Put the rolls in the oven, pour 1 cup of hot water into the empty pan to create steam, and quickly close the door.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped, then cool on a rack.

original.title: Zwiebelkuchen (Onion Tart)
original.description: A savory autumn tart of slow-cooked onions, bacon and caraway in a creamy custard, traditionally served with new wine (Federweißer).
steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, add the milk and butter, and knead into a soft dough; cover and let rise for 45 minutes.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet until it renders its fat, then add the butter and onions.
Cook the onions over medium-low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and golden; let cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a 10 x 15-inch rimmed baking sheet or a 12-inch tart pan.
Roll the dough out and press it into the pan, forming a small rim.
Whisk the sour cream, eggs, caraway, salt and pepper, then stir in the onion mixture.
Spread the filling evenly over the dough.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the filling is set and golden brown, then let rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
